the development of a novel vaccination strategy for the induction of primary tumor antigen specific T‐lymphocy‐te responses in breast cancer patients after high dose chemotherapy with PBPCT.
the development of novel vaccination strategies for the treatment of patients with breast or ovarian cancer after high‐doses chemotherapy and autologeous PBPC transplantation.

DC‐based cancer vaccines have the potential to be a promising approach to the treatment of minimal residual disease.

the clinical application of DC‐based vaccines in patients after PBPCT is feasible and safe, but further clinical studies are necessary to prove the clinical relevance and the immunogenicity of DC‐based cancer vaccines in patients after high‐ dose chemotherapy and autologoues PBPCT.
DC‐based immunotherapy after high‐doses of chemotherapy and PBPCT is a novel, promising and feasible treatment strategy for the eradication of MRD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DC‐based immunotherapy after PBPCT is feasible, and that the induction of primary CTL responses can be achieved.

the induction of primary CTL responses in vivo is possible, and that the generation of DC from CD34+ cells is superior to that from monocytes.
